original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Independent conditional audit of PR3620 (head 5a4354c6) PROOF.md sections 1 and 3: given PR3609's changed full dual (head 13f974da) and the named paired-chain coverage law, does deleting at most 425 rank units per dual call fail for every pair count, does 426 pass, is the coverage grant favourable without double counting, and how should the stated 4.557-unit slack be quoted?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a chronological side-correction program. The family expansion gate stops further P104 construction until the complete cost allowance is specified. The newest unreviewed P104 numeric gate (PR3620's 425/426 threshold on PR3609's dual) is the current optimistic necessary condition on that allowance, so auditing it is the live missing obligation; no correction word is synthesised here.
bottleneck_link: Checks the deletion threshold and the optimistic slack ceiling (a necessary condition, not a realised allowance) that a realised P104 correction acting by rank-unit deletion must meet before the stopped P104 supplier can reopen (research-family-status expansion gate). Confirms 426 rank units per dual call as the least uniform per-call deletion that passes; the excess depends only on the total deletion, so uneven calls need a total of at least 7*425+3 = 2978 at p=7 (some call above 425). Under the retained limiting conversion kappa = a/(1+a) (bottleneck-brief.md) an improvement needs a > a_req = kappa/(1-kappa), so the sharp ceilings are the values at a_req (suprema, not attained): a cost proportional to dual calls is best at p=7 (0.710094 per dual call at a_req, 0.651010 at PR3620's 1/596); a purely fixed cost is best at p=8 (5.524500 at a_req, 5.040108 at 1/596); a mixed cost c0 + c1*p passes iff c0 + c1*p < -E426(p,a) for some p. PR3620's 4.557071 seven-pair slack is correct as scoped. Values at a = kappa are looser rejection-side figures (RESULT.json).
stop_rule: Stop when source binding, the coverage-grant check, the reductions and the arithmetic are each marked confirmed/clarified/refuted with a reproducer for any defect; no new consumers, networks or downstream extensions; one verify round plus at most one revise round.
evidence: verify.py: 31 exact claims. The d<=425 rejection is proved by two methods (A: Fraction intervals on the clamped model plus convexity; B: Decimal closed form at p=1..23 plus a linear tail from p=24); the passing points E426(7,1/596) and E428(4,1/596) are checked by both methods; the kappa points, passing ranges and slack comparisons use method A (plus convexity for the ranges). E425(6,7,8; kappa) = 2.623221066338944..., 1.600686410509596..., 1.973543616715320...; E426(7,1/596) = -4.557071360876949...; E426(7,kappa) = -5.455691507045708...; E427(4,kappa) = 1.740333669596917...; E428(4,1/596) = -1.822408282623730... (values truncated toward zero; enclosures in RESULT.json). d=426 passes at p=6..10 (a=1/596) and p=6..11 (kappa/(1-kappa), kappa); slack per dual call is maximal at p=7 (0.710094403780 at kappa/(1-kappa), 0.651010194410 at 1/596), total slack at p=8 (5.524500277810 at kappa/(1-kappa), 5.040108017937 at 1/596). controls.py: 14 mutations each break a named claim, positive control passes. REVIEW.md: every step valid/confirmed; 3.11 and 3.12 valid as scoped and clarified.

open_questions.question: Which ceiling form should P104 gates quote: the per-dual-call ceiling (binding at p=7) or the fixed-cost ceiling (binding at p=8)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The requirement itself is fixed by the retained conversion (a > kappa/(1-kappa)). For exactly 426 deletions the sharp ceilings at a_req are 0.710094 per dual call (p=7) and 5.524500 fixed (p=8); a gate quoting the wrong form can misjudge a proposal; quoting values at kappa can wrongly accept, and quoting values at 1/596 can wrongly reject.
open_questions.first_step: Quote both sharp ceilings at a_req in docs/research/research-family-status.md, with the mixed-cost rule c0 + c1*p < -E426(p,a) for some p.
open_questions.blocked_by: Maintainer edit of the family status file; no computation needed.

open_questions.question: Can a realised deletion network remove at least 426 rank units per dual call from PR3609's dual within the optimistic ceiling (for exactly 426 rank-one deletions and a purely per-call cost, less than about 0.71 normalised units per dual call)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the optimistic ceiling under the named law (a_req = kappa/(1-kappa), best pair count p=7) for a correction acting by rank-unit deletion from D; each further rank-one deletion per dual call adds 121^a, about 1.008 units per dual call at p=7. For a correction applied identically in every dual call, failing it keeps that route stopped; uneven calls must meet the total threshold instead. Other replacement profiles must pass PR3620 section 2's general criterion.
open_questions.first_step: Name 426 removable rank-one children of PR3609's dual and their endpoint contracts before any pricing.
open_questions.blocked_by: No candidate deletion network exists; the coverage law itself is unrealised.
